integration.summary: Full code-trace verification of Figma -> frontend -> API -> business logic -> DB vertical slice for Finding Detail, matching the M04 integration bar. Type contract match confirmed: finding-detail-client.tsx's FindingDetail import is the exact same type re-exported from lib/findings.ts (no local re-declaration, no `any`, no field-name drift) -- id/repoFullName/filePath/commitSha/matchedRule/redactedSnippet/status/createdAt all match exactly, including that commitSha here is the FULL sha (not the 7-char short form used by FindingSummary in the list). Request paths traced end-to-end for all three routes: GET/POST handlers call requireSession() first and return 401 immediately on failure, before any Prisma call -- confirmed by reading route.ts/approve/route.ts/ignore/route.ts line-by-line and by the auth-boundary tests (401 cases) exercising the real handler with a null-session mock. No data read/written pre-auth in any of the three routes. approveFinding/ignoreFinding transition logic re-derived by hand: both do an initial findUnique for a fast/clear 404 or 409, then the authoritative mutation is a conditional `updateMany({ where: { id, status: 'PENDING' }, data: { status: X } })` -- Postgres evaluates this as a single atomic statement, so two concurrent requests can never both match/affect the same row while PENDING; the loser's `result.count === 0` path re-reads and throws InvalidFindingTransitionError (409), never silently succeeds or double-transitions. This is genuinely race-safe at the DB level, not just TOCTOU-guarded in application code. findings-client.tsx's two new <Link href={`/findings/${finding.id}`}> call sites (desktop table + mobile card) verified to use the real per-row finding.id (not a static/stale path), and the route they point to (app/(protected)/findings/[id]/page.tsx) exists and builds -- no repeat of M04's fixed /dashboard/findings-style bug. Confirm Approve dialog's Approve & Flag button calls handleApproveConfirm -> POST .../approve and awaits the JSON body before closing; on !res.ok it sets a visible role=alert banner with the server's message (or a generic fallback) and closes the modal without throwing; the Ignore button's handleIgnore similarly POSTs, is wrapped in try/catch, and surfaces the same alert banner on failure or network error -- no unhandled promise rejection in either path (both fetches are awaited inside try/catch/finally, loading flags always reset in finally). 401/404 cases were not separately hand-tested against the live UI (no browser/dev server available in this environment) but the client's generic catch-all (`!res.ok` -> setActionError) covers 401/404/409 identically at the code level; a session-expired 401 would surface the same inline banner rather than crash. redactedSnippet traced end-to-end with zero re-processing: Prisma select -> toFindingDetail() straight passthrough (no string ops) -> JSON.stringify by NextResponse.json -> client useState(initialFinding) -> rendered as a plain JSX text node ({finding.redactedSnippet}, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, no template concatenation that could drop redaction characters). Grepped all new/changed findings files for console.log/error/warn/debug -- zero matches; grepped for realistic raw-secret patterns (AKIA without redaction dots, ghp_, sk_live_ without dots) across route/test files -- only present inside already-redacted test fixtures, matching the redaction tests' own intent. Full command matrix run together (not in isolation): apps/web typecheck (tsc --noEmit) clean, apps/web lint (next lint) clean, apps/web vitest run 9 files / 62 tests passed (up from M04's 41 -- confirms the +21 new M05 tests: 5 detail GET, 8 approve, 8 ignore -- all passing alongside the pre-existing M02/M03/M04 suites with zero regressions), apps/web production build succeeded with dummy env vars and registers ƒ /api/findings/[id], ƒ /api/findings/[id]/approve, ƒ /api/findings/[id]/ignore, and ƒ /findings/[id] as dynamic routes. apps/worker typecheck and its 3 test files / 24 tests also re-run and confirmed unaffected (M05 does not touch apps/worker, verified by changedFiles list and by the fact apps/worker has no findings-detail-related code). Prisma schema confirmed unchanged: `prisma validate` passes, and apps/web/prisma/migrations/ still ends at 20260816140000_add_finding_dedup_constraint (M04's last migration) -- no new migration directory was created by this module, matching backend-builder's claim of zero schema drift; Finding.id is a plain String cuid column (no strict UUID validation at the DB layer), so an arbitrary/malformed :id path segment safely resolves to Prisma returning null (-> clean 404) rather than throwing, in both the detail GET and the two action POSTs. Navigation verified: sidebar's 'Findings' nav item (pre-existing, unchanged by M05) points at /findings and stays highlighted via startsWith() while on a /findings/[id] detail page too; the detail page's '← Findings' back-link and the ErrorState's retry path both resolve to real, already-verified routes; the two updated findings-client.tsx View links resolve to the real, newly-built /findings/[id] route -- no 404 dead ends introduced by this module. Pre-existing unrelated sidebar links (Review Queue, Scan Rules, Flags, Workers, Templates, Users, Settings) remain unbuilt dead links from earlier/future modules, out of M05's scope, not a regression introduced here.
notedGaps: No live Postgres/Redis instance available in this environment -- all verification above is via mocked-Prisma vitest tests, tsc/eslint static analysis, and a successful `next build`; true end-to-end runtime execution (real DB round-trip, real session cookie, real browser click-through of Approve/Ignore/Confirm modal, real 401 redirect-to-sign-in behavior) remains a pre-production follow-up, consistent with M04's own noted gap.

security.summary: Reviewed raw-secret exposure surface, authorization boundaries on all three routes, state-transition race safety, audit logging content, and XSS surface for Finding Detail. No raw secret/token exposure found anywhere: redactedSnippet is read-only passthrough of an already-redacted value, never re-processed, never logged (zero console.* calls across all M05 files). Race-safety confirmed genuine at the DB layer via conditional updateMany. Audit logging captures userId/action/detail(findingId), verified free of raw secret patterns. Error responses (401/403/404/409) return only generic codes/messages, no internal detail leakage. All rendered fields are plain JSX text, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML. Confirm Approve dialog prevents double-submission via loading/disabled state. BLOCKING issue found and resolved during this review (see below) before DONE.
security.blockingIssueFound: POST /api/findings/:id/approve and /ignore were initially gated behind requireSession() (any authenticated USER), not requireAdmin(). ARCHITECTURE.md places 'review/approve queue' and 'approve -> flag' under the Admin Panel (role=admin) and states the admin review gate should be ON by default (also CLAUDE.md section 8); docs/MODULES.md lists approve/ignore/audit-trail under M06 Admin Review Queue. Flagged to the user as a stop-condition (security-sensitive authorization decision, not silently resolved) per CLAUDE.md section 11.
security.resolution: User explicitly chose to gate approve/ignore to requireAdmin() now (2026-08-16). Both routes updated to use the existing lib/authorize.ts requireAdmin() helper, returning 401 (unauthenticated) vs 403 (forbidden, authenticated non-admin) distinctly. Route tests updated (403-for-USER, 200-for-ADMIN cases added, replacing the old 'any authenticated user' assertions). Frontend (findings/[id]/page.tsx) now reads the server session role and passes isAdmin to FindingDetailClient, which hides the Approve/Ignore actions for non-admin users (defense-in-depth UX only -- the server route is the real, independently-enforced boundary). Full apps/web command matrix (typecheck/lint/test/build) re-run clean after the fix: 64 tests passing (+2 for the new 403/200 role cases), production build succeeds with all four /api/findings/:id* routes + /findings/[id] registered.
followUps: LOW: apps/web/app/api/findings/[id]/route.ts has no try/catch around getFindingDetail() -- an unhandled Prisma error falls through to Next's default handler. Pre-existing repo-wide gap (same as /api/tokens, GET /api/findings), not an M05-specific regression.
LOW: Finding Detail page.tsx treats a 404 (finding not found) identically to a transient load failure (both render the generic ErrorState/Retry UI) -- UX correctness follow-up, not a security issue.

LOW: Flagged state's IssueReferenceRow renders a generic placeholder rather than a real issue URL/number (Finding has no issueUrl column yet, M07 scope) -- confirmed this never fabricates or exposes any URL/secret-adjacent value.
LOW: No rate limiting on POST /approve or /ignore beyond the PENDING-only one-shot transition guard -- worth folding into M13 Hardening's global rate-limiting pass.

checks.note: The figma-auditor subagent's result arrived after a delay and was reconciled against the live Figma file (each claim independently re-verified via use_figma before any fix was applied). It found 2 BLOCKING issues, both confirmed and fixed: (1) Header instance was stuck at its 960px default width instead of stretching to the full 1440px frame width in 6 of 7 non-mobile frames (33:636 Pending, 34:700 Loading, 34:748 Error, 35:694 Approved, 36:726 Flagged, 37:844 Confirm Approve) — fixed via resize(1440, height); verified the Header's internal 'Right' sub-frame (search/theme-switcher/avatar) auto-repositions to hug the new right edge (x=1132, right edge=1420) exactly like M02's (15:39) and M04's (28:454) Header instances. (2) The Error state (34:694) used a hand-built 'Error Panel' frame (34:780) instead of reusing the shared Error State component (7:92) the way M02 (15:611) and M04 (30:605) do — fixed by removing the hand-built panel and creating a live Error State instance (new node 40:859, resized to 1136x184 matching M04's pattern) with copy overridden to 'Failed to load finding' / "We couldn't load this finding. Please try again." Also applied 4 non-blocking cleanups the auditor flagged: renamed generic 'Frame' field-row labels to descriptive names (Repository/File/Commit/Rule Row, Code Snippet Block, Actions, Issue Reference Row) in Approved/Flagged/Ignored to match Pending's naming; standardized all Badge instances to 'Status Badge' (was inconsistently 'Badge' on Approved/Flagged/Ignored/Mobile); removed redundant opacity:0.5 overrides on 3 button instances (35:752, 35:754, 37:814) that were already correctly instanced from the library's real Disabled variants (4:22, 4:10) — the opacity was double-dimming an already-disabled-styled component, not compensating for a missing one. Post-fix re-verification: 0 overlap pairs across all 27 page frames (unchanged), 199 text nodes re-scanned for realistic secret patterns (0 matches, unchanged), all 6 Header instances confirmed at width=1440, Error State instance confirmed linked to main component 7:92. Full findings list from the auditor is not independently reproduced verbatim here since each item was re-verified first-hand rather than taken on faith; the concrete before/after state for every item is recorded above.

'Dashboard / Finding Detail / Failed' (docs/figma/SCREEN_INVENTORY.md item 20, representing Finding.status=FAILED) was NOT designed in this pass. If the product still needs a dedicated Finding Detail view for status=FAILED findings (distinct from a load-error), that remains an open design gap against the screen inventory and should be scoped explicitly in a follow-up task.
